newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's travel account balance improves in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Canada's travel account balance improves in Q1.

text.p: Canada's international travel account balance improved in the first quarter of 1997, with the deficit falling 5.0 percent from the previous quarter, Statistics Canada said on Friday.

The international travel account balance -- the difference between receipts and payments -- was in a deficit position of C$714 million, down from C$752 million in the fourth quarter of 1996, the federal agency said.
Foreign visitors to Canada injected a record C$3.2 billion into the Canadian economy in the first quarter of 1997, Statistics Canada said.
The spending was an increase of 4.1 percent from the fourth quarter of 1996.
Canadian travelers also broke a record in the first quarter, spending C$3.9 billion abroad, a 2.3 percent increase, Statistics Canada said.
The deficit reached its most recent low of C$602 million in the second quarter of 1996 after peaking at C$1.9 billion in the fourth quarter of 1991.
The travel account deficit with the United States fell for a second consecutive quarter, reaching C$786 million for the first quarter of 1997.

Visitors to Canada from countries other than the United States outspent Canadians traveling to overseas countries in the first three months of 1997. Overseas residents spent C$1.5 billion in Canada, a slight decrease from the previous quarter, StatsCan said.
Canadians spent a record C$1.4 billion overseas, up 1.0 percent.
